title: First-Bloom and Phenology Shift Calendar
dataSources: Seismograph events (`seismograph:event`), seismic noise (`seismograph:noise`), air quality (`airquality:reading`), radiation counts (`radiation:count`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), phenology observations (`phenology:observation`), and weather-station rainfall (`weatherstation:reading`).
app: Citizen-science telemetry from seismographs, weather stations, air-quality monitors, Geiger counters, lightning feeds, and phenology journals streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=phenology:observation event="first_bloom"
| eval year=strftime(_time,"%Y")
| stats earliest(_time) as first_seen by species year
| eval day_of_year=strftime(first_seen,"%j")
| sort species year
description: Tracks the first bloom day of year for each species so seasonal shifts are visible across multiple years.
value: A simple first-bloom calendar turns garden notes into longitudinal citizen-science evidence of changing seasonal timing.
implementation: Log bloom-start observations with species names and keep the same naming conventions year after year.
visualization: Line chart of first-bloom day by species and year.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces when each plant first flowers each year, which helps you see if the seasons are shifting over time.
